typical_causes: Third-party payment gateway service provider outage.
Expired SSL/TLS client certificates or authentication API tokens.
Connection socket timeouts under high concurrency loads.
fix_steps: Check the external status page of upstream payment providers (e.g., Stripe, PayPal).
Verify gateway connection credentials and validate token expiration status.
Trigger failover script to route traffic through the secondary payment partner.
Restart the payment processor container to clear hung sockets.
user_message_template: We are experiencing temporary difficulties processing credit card payments. Our engineers are investigating. Your billing details are safe; please wait before retrying.

typical_causes: Database server disk storage exhaustion.
Connection pool exhaustion due to leaking transactions.
Unoptimized query locking database index files.
Hardware failure or network partition on DB cluster node.
fix_steps: Check disk space usage on the primary database host.
Analyze connection counts and terminate orphaned client connections.
Identify and kill long-running exclusive locks in the process list.
Failover database primary node to a hot replica state.
user_message_template: We are undergoing emergency database maintenance. Some account services, shopping carts, and history logs may be temporarily offline. We expect full recovery shortly.

typical_causes: Downstream inventory, address verification, or shipping API degradation.
Misconfigured gateway client socket timeout values.
High downstream latency causing local server worker starvation.
DNS resolution failure for partner endpoints.
fix_steps: Identify the specific downstream integration route causing latency.
Verify DNS resolution and network path latency to downstream hosts.
Temporarily lower local socket timeout thresholds to fail fast.
Enable circuit breaker overrides to bypass non-critical integrations.
user_message_template: An integrated partner service is taking longer than usual to respond. Some functions may load slowly. We are modifying route priorities to bypass the delay.

typical_causes: Syntax errors introduced in a recent deployment release.
Broken upstream dependency or package configuration changes.
Environment variable or credentials mismatch in system config.
Heavy load causing service threshold limits to exhaust (HTTP 429/503).
fix_steps: Check server deployment version logs and pull recent Git commit diffs.
Verify system environment variables and secrets are populated correctly.
Trigger automated rollback to the last stable deployment revision.
Scale up container instances to distribute application traffic load.
user_message_template: We are experiencing an elevated frequency of errors across our systems. We have initiated a rollback to restore stability and regret the inconvenience.

typical_causes: Database inventory table locking preventing stock changes.
Discrepancies in cart item payload parsing on checkout routes.
Corrupted item session caches in Redis or local memory.
fix_steps: Check database lock queues and verify inventory table health.
Inspect checkout logs for JSON payload serialization issues.
Flush temporary cart cache clusters and verify schema validation rules.
Restart the checkout API instance to clear locked cart threads.
user_message_template: We detected an error while finalizing your order checkout. Your cart items have been saved. Please refresh the page or try completing the checkout in a few minutes.

typical_causes: Redis session backend container is offline or unreachable.
JWT key rotation failure or expired cryptographic secrets.
Auth database service capacity overload or slow read speeds.
fix_steps: Verify Redis container status and check network accessibility.
Check authentication token secrets configurations in environment files.
Monitor read latency on the credentials database table.
Scale session and token validation nodes to handle high login demand.
user_message_template: We are experiencing issues processing user sign-ins and session validations. Active sessions are safe. Please hold on while we reconnect the identity server.

typical_causes: High CPU/Memory usage on core API worker instances.
Network routing issues within the internal VPC cluster.
Slow database disk I/O performance on read queries.
fix_steps: Analyze resource usage metrics across nodes (CPU, RAM, load averages).
Scale server resource capacity using horizontal auto-scaling rules.
Deploy read replicas to reduce queries on primary database server.
Reroute network traffic paths within regional clusters.
user_message_template: Our platform is currently operating at reduced speeds. Page loading times may be higher than average. We are scaling resources to bring speeds back to normal.

typical_causes: App debug logging level generating excessive file writes.
Failure of cron log rotation jobs on system servers.
Orphaned temporary download files remaining in directories.
fix_steps: Locate the largest directories using disk usage commands.
Verify logrotate processes are running and trigger manual rotation.
Clean temp folders and delete orphaned Docker images/volumes.
Re-allocate or expand target storage disk volume partitions.
user_message_template: We are currently conducting preventative maintenance on our storage storage cluster. Service is operational, but temporary files may process slower than normal.
